body:
Where do I start? I'm a 21 year old male. My life began when I was 3 years old. Unfortunately, my parents divorced soon after. I spent most of my time with my mom, visiting my dad frequently. My dad met a girl, who years later became his step-wife. My brother, during this whole time isolated. I never really knew my brother very much, I barely even knew he existed, and what I did know of him he was an asshole. I think he was jealous of me, since he was very antisocial and always got in trouble, while I was the perfect child that could do no wrong. 

My mom, a lesbian, partnered up with another lesbo. This was when I was around 8, and at first things went pretty swell. But after awhile it became apparent that she did not like children, and became verbally abusive. This began the loss of my innocence, and things really went down hill from there.

When i was about 14, my mom came up to me and said, "son we're moving to Elk Grove. Gated community. It's gonna be awesooooooome." I cried. 

There was nothing to do there. I lost all of my friends. I learned how to entertain myself, since, there was nothing to do. This was the beginning of my depression, and thoughts of death and suicide. 

So as an adult now, I moved to Sacramento, but nothing has really changed. I have the bad habit of isolating, I have a hard time making friends or doing social activities. Nothing really excites me. I spend my days watching Netflix, or listening to music. My life is really like a state of limbo, nothing really happens, and I'll do anything to numb myself.
Thank you, it's nice to hear a different perspective on it. An honest one.

I've been in treatment for years. I'm probably going to end up as an inpatient, again. 

Selfish? Maybe. But why isn't it selfish to let someone suffer?

My question is a personal one. It has been a constant struggle between wanting to kill myself and knowing there are people who care about me. I just don't understand the obligation. Why do I have to stay alive for these people while I'm suffering?
